domain.name: Resources, Competence & Awareness
domain.description: Assesses whether the organization provides the resources, competence, awareness, training, and communication needed to support information security and ISMS readiness.
domain.sourceNote: Questions are independently authored for readiness assessment and do not reproduce ISO standard text.

coreQuestions.question: Has your organization identified the resources needed to establish, operate, and improve its information security program?
coreQuestions.helpText: This checks whether security readiness has realistic support through people, tools, budget, time, external support, and management attention.

coreQuestions.question: Has your organization identified the competence needed for people whose work affects information security?
coreQuestions.helpText: This verifies whether the organization knows which skills are needed for IT administration, security operations, risk ownership, incident response, access management, and policy ownership.

coreQuestions.question: Does your organization provide security awareness or training to relevant employees and contractors?
coreQuestions.helpText: This checks whether people understand common risks, security rules, acceptable use, incident reporting, and their responsibilities.

coreQuestions.question: Are personnel aware of the information security policy and their individual responsibilities?
coreQuestions.helpText: This verifies whether employees and contractors know the rules they are expected to follow and understand how their actions affect security.

coreQuestions.question: Has the organization defined how information security communication is handled internally and externally?
coreQuestions.helpText: This checks whether the organization knows what to communicate, when to communicate, who communicates, and which channels are used for security topics.

coreQuestions.question: Does your organization keep evidence of competence, awareness, training, or communication activities?
coreQuestions.helpText: This verifies whether the organization can show evidence that people are trained, competent, and informed about security responsibilities.

sectorQuestions.question: Do engineering, DevOps, and support teams receive security training relevant to SaaS product security and customer data protection?
sectorQuestions.helpText: SaaS teams need awareness of secure development, production access, incident reporting, secrets handling, customer data protection, and support access rules.

sectorQuestions.question: Are developers and technical staff competent in secure coding, cloud security basics, access management, and incident escalation?
sectorQuestions.helpText: This checks whether the people building and operating the SaaS platform have the skills needed to reduce product and infrastructure security risks.

sectorQuestions.question: Are security communications integrated into engineering workflows such as release planning, incident reviews, and product updates?
sectorQuestions.helpText: Security communication should reach the teams that make changes to the product, infrastructure, and customer-facing services.
expectedEvidence: Security updates in sprint or roadmap notes

sectorQuestions.question: Do employees handling payments, transactions, customer onboarding, or fraud-related workflows receive relevant security training?
sectorQuestions.helpText: Fintech teams should understand risks related to financial data, transaction integrity, fraud exposure, account compromise, and regulatory expectations.

sectorQuestions.question: Are staff responsible for financial systems competent in access control, transaction security, audit trail handling, and incident escalation?
sectorQuestions.helpText: This checks whether key personnel have the skills needed to operate and protect financial workflows and supporting systems.

sectorQuestions.question: Are security communications defined for financial incidents, fraud indicators, provider issues, and customer-impacting events?
sectorQuestions.helpText: Fintech organizations need clear communication paths for events that may affect money movement, customer trust, and financial service continuity.

sectorQuestions.question: Do clinical, administrative, and IT staff receive security awareness appropriate to patient information and healthcare operations?
sectorQuestions.helpText: Healthcare personnel should understand patient information protection, account security, device use, confidentiality, and incident reporting.

sectorQuestions.question: Are staff responsible for clinical systems and patient records competent in secure access, confidentiality, and incident escalation?
sectorQuestions.helpText: This checks whether personnel operating sensitive healthcare systems have the competence needed to protect patient services and information.

sectorQuestions.question: Are communication procedures defined for incidents affecting patient information, clinical availability, or external medical partners?
sectorQuestions.helpText: Healthcare incidents can affect confidentiality and service continuity, so communication responsibilities and escalation paths should be clear.

sectorQuestions.question: Do store administrators, support, marketing, and fulfillment teams receive security awareness relevant to customer accounts and order information?
sectorQuestions.helpText: E-commerce teams should understand customer information handling, account security, payment-related risks, fraud indicators, and safe use of store tools.

sectorQuestions.question: Are staff responsible for the online store competent in admin access management, payment-related workflows, and incident escalation?
sectorQuestions.helpText: This checks whether personnel operating the e-commerce platform understand the controls needed to protect store operations and customer trust.

sectorQuestions.question: Are communication procedures defined for store downtime, account compromise, fraud indicators, or customer-impacting security events?
sectorQuestions.helpText: E-commerce incidents can quickly affect customer trust, so teams need clear internal and external communication paths.

sectorQuestions.question: Do teachers, administrative staff, and IT staff receive security awareness relevant to student records, exams, and learning platforms?
sectorQuestions.helpText: Education staff should understand secure handling of student information, exam integrity, account security, cloud tools, and incident reporting.

sectorQuestions.question: Are staff responsible for student systems, exam platforms, and learning tools competent in secure access and incident escalation?
sectorQuestions.helpText: This checks whether key staff have the competence needed to operate education platforms securely.

sectorQuestions.question: Are communication procedures defined for student information incidents, platform downtime, or exam system issues?
sectorQuestions.helpText: Education organizations need clear communication paths for incidents affecting students, teachers, parents, and administration.

sectorQuestions.question: Do NOC, support, field, maintenance, and IT teams receive security awareness relevant to network operations and customer connectivity?
sectorQuestions.helpText: Telecom and network teams should understand secure access, configuration change risks, incident escalation, physical site risks, and provider dependencies.

sectorQuestions.question: Are personnel responsible for network infrastructure competent in access control, configuration management, monitoring, and incident response?
sectorQuestions.helpText: This checks whether network operations personnel have the competence needed to protect infrastructure and respond to security events.

sectorQuestions.question: Are communication procedures defined for network outages, infrastructure incidents, upstream provider issues, and customer-impacting events?
sectorQuestions.helpText: Telecom security communication should support fast escalation and clear coordination during operational and security incidents.

sectorQuestions.question: Do consultants, contractors, freelancers, and project staff receive security awareness relevant to client confidentiality and project workspaces?
sectorQuestions.helpText: Professional services teams should understand confidentiality, secure collaboration, client file handling, remote work, and access responsibilities.

sectorQuestions.name: Resources, Competence & Awareness
sectorQuestions.question: Are staff handling client deliverables competent in secure file handling, access control, remote work security, and incident escalation?
sectorQuestions.helpText: This checks whether people handling client work have the competence needed to protect confidential project information.

sectorQuestions.question: Are communication procedures defined for client confidentiality incidents, project access issues, or collaboration platform problems?
sectorQuestions.helpText: Professional services organizations need clear communication for issues that could affect clients, contracts, and project delivery.

sectorQuestions.question: Do employees receive basic awareness on passwords, email threats, device security, backups, and incident reporting?
sectorQuestions.helpText: For SMEs, awareness can start with simple and practical topics that reduce the most common security risks.

sectorQuestions.question: Is the person responsible for IT or security competent enough to manage accounts, backups, devices, updates, and provider coordination?
sectorQuestions.helpText: This checks whether the responsible person, internal or external, has the practical competence needed to support basic security readiness.

sectorQuestions.question: Does the company have a simple communication path for security issues, IT problems, suspicious emails, or lost devices?
sectorQuestions.helpText: Small companies need a clear and simple way for people to report issues quickly.

selectionLogic.description: For each company, return all core questions plus the sector-specific questions matching the company's sector.
